title: Nine Words of Leading
subtitle: 互助关爱 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）
meta: 主题语境：互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）　|　核心词汇：cheer　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cheer 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 my mother was sent to lead ① cheer she could not hear, and she said the leading was the whole of the lesson. The ② cheer, meaning the shout and not the comfort, was nine words long and was led by whoever came last; cheer, she said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ cheer in that hall had the same beat, and the ④ cheer at the end, meaning the one the captain kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever led properly. Cheer, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ cheer was the whole of the visit, meaning the comfort it carried and not the shout. The ⑥ cheer, meaning the comfort and not any of that, is the only thing in a visit that everybody needs and nobody questions; cheer, he said, is either something you lead or the only word that means both a shout and a comfort. She said the comfort is the part they remember.

By 1973 the ⑦ cheer had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the beat. The ⑧ cheer of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine words and eleven years of leading; cheer, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ cheer I remember is the one at the end, which was led in 1978 and is still described as the loudest in the county. A ⑩ cheer, my grandmother said in 1983, is the only thing that improves by being led; every cheer, she said, is a comfort that has agreed to look like a shout. She said the comfort was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 欢呼（指那一声呼喊本身，与那份安慰相对）
C. 固定搭配：lead a cheer 领一声欢呼
D. n. 欢呼（指那座大厅里每一声）
E. n. 欢呼（指末尾那一声）
F. n. 鼓舞（抽象：它承载的那份安慰）
G. n. 那份安慰（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The cheer, meaning the shout and not the comfort
cheer was the whole of the visit
the cheer had become a number in a report
The cheer of the whole thing

answers.why: lead a cheer 意为“领一声欢呼”，1958 年母亲被派去领她听不见的那声欢呼。
cheer 意为“欢呼、喝彩”，指那一声呼喊本身而不是那份安慰，共九个词，由最后来的人领。
cheer 指那座大厅里每一声欢呼，每一声都是同样的节拍。
cheer 指末尾那一声（队长保留的那一声），是唯一有人认真领过的。
cheer 意为“鼓舞”，抽象指它承载的那份安慰，父亲说 cheer 就是那次探望的全部。
cheer 为抽象用法，指那份安慰本身，是一次探望里人人都需要、却没人质疑的东西。
cheer 意为“欢呼、喝彩”，到 1973 年这声 cheer 成了报告里的一个数字。
cheer 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九个词和十一年的领喊。
cheer 意为“欢呼”，我记得的是末尾那一声，1978 年领过，至今仍被说成全县最响的。
cheer 为抽象总称，祖母说一声欢呼是唯一会因为被认真领喊而变好的东西。
